chunk_findings.detail: The decision gives incompatible scopes for the docs check and then registers `README.md` in a way that makes both readings fail. Point (5) says `ddflow docs check` runs on “classed or changed docs only, never the whole README at once” because checking this README measured >120s, while point (6) says the docs check visits “classed AND changed docs only.” Step 2 registers `README.md` as classed evergreen. If implementers follow the “classed or changed” rule, `README.md` is classed and therefore checked by the docs gate, which is exactly the whole-README check the same paragraph says must not happen and would hit the >120s wall. If they follow the “classed AND changed” rule, a classed-but-unchanged `README.md` is not checked, contradicting the claim that a `[docs.classes]` entry implies the docs check and allowing stale classed docs to pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `--reason` argument is emitted as a space-separated option (`--reason '<value>'`) and is only shell-quoted. If the findings summary’s first line is a single token that begins with a dash, e.g. `--bug`, the printed line becomes `... --reason '--bug'`. When that line is parsed as a command (the same `shlex.split` + `cli.build_parser().parse_args` path used by the regression test), the shell-style quotes are removed and argparse sees `--reason` followed by `--bug`. Argparse treats `--bug` as another option, not as the value for `--reason`, so `gate record` parsing still fails (or records no reason) for that valid findings text. The added test uses `a bug`, which contains a space and therefore avoids the argparse option-value ambiguity, so it does not catch this. Emitting `--reason=<shlex.quote(summary)>` would keep the value attached to the option.

data.summary: Bug fix tasks for ddflow-itself bugs default to project-wide globs, observed as ddflow/** plus tests/** on auto-filed fix tasks. Two narrow parallel bug fixes then exclude each other, and a dead sibling holding that default kept ddflow/** and tests/** exclusively for over 20 minutes, refusing commits that touched two narrow files and serializing the whole wave. fix-bug tasks should default to the bug's own found scope (the files the bug record names plus the tests that pin them), with the current wide default reserved for bugs that name many files.
data.title: Wide default fix-task globs serialize the wave

data.body:
Fixes bug B45b80286d2: Bug fix tasks for ddflow-itself bugs default to project-wide globs, observed as ddflow/** plus tests/** on auto-filed fix tasks. Two narrow parallel bug fixes then exclude each other, and a dead sibling holding that default kept ddflow/** and tests/** exclusively for over 20 minutes, refusing commits that touched two narrow files and serializing the whole wave. fix-bug tasks should default to the bug's own found scope (the files the bug record names plus the tests that pin them), with the current wide default reserved for bugs that name many files.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B45b80286d2 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B45b80286d2 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B45b80286d2: Wide default fix-task globs serialize the wave

data.summary: After a merge deletes the item worktree, the unit_tests gate in practice refuses to run: it says gates run before merge. A wave merged fix-B74d5c39e6e with every other gate green and post-merge ci passed, then complete refused forever on required gate unit_tests unavailable, with no agent-attainable verb recording the honest outcome. Operator-only routes remain force, a person's path. Merge should capture the unfilled gate state when it deletes the worktree, or complete must accept the post-merge tree as an outcome home, or a gate record unavailable post-merge with a stored reason must arm the refusal to lay out clearly.
data.title: Merged item cannot complete: unit_tests refuses post-merge worktree removal

data.body:
Fixes bug B430dae3a68: After a merge deletes the item worktree, the unit_tests gate in practice refuses to run: it says gates run before merge. A wave merged fix-B74d5c39e6e with every other gate green and post-merge ci passed, then complete refused forever on required gate unit_tests unavailable, with no agent-attainable verb recording the honest outcome. Operator-only routes remain force, a person's path. Merge should capture the unfilled gate state when it deletes the worktree, or complete must accept the post-merge tree as an outcome home, or a gate record unavailable post-merge with a stored reason must arm the refusal to lay out clearly.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B430dae3a68 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B430dae3a68 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B430dae3a68: Merged item cannot complete: unit_tests refuses post-merge worktree removal

chunk_findings.detail: The decision makes `README.md` a classed evergreen doc (point 3, line 15) and says the docs gate runs `ddflow docs check` only on “classed AND changed docs” (point 5, line 19; point 6, line 21), while also saying the only whole-README run is a one-off inside `readme-manage` step 2 and “not a per-item cost.” But point 1 (line 11) and point 4 (line 17) keep the primary README’s hand sections — agent brief, benefits, workflow at a glance — in `README.md` and say their owning items edit them normally; point 5 also says generated rows/tables stay in `README.md` and are regenerated from later fragments. Given any normal item that edits one of those primary hand sections, or any item whose fragment change regenerates a README table, `README.md` is both classed and changed, so the docs gate must run the docs check on the whole 6700-line README for that item. That is exactly the >120s cost the decision says should be a one-off, not per item; the decision does not specify a fragment-scoped docs check or an exclusion that prevents this.

chunk_findings.detail: The item-scoped assertions can pass on a useless self-only or empty-row result. With `floor=0.10`, a record compared with itself is maximally similar, so if `pair_records` scores/returns only `("R149", "R149")`, the first test passes: `asked` is non-empty, every scored pair contains `R149`, and `all(... for r in rows)` is true. It is also vacuously true for `rows` if the hook fires but no rows are returned. The 3000-record test at line 92 has the same gap: it passes if `rows` is only `[{"a": "R1499", "b": "R1499"}]`. Thus the regression test would not catch a fix that only self-matches the asked item or drops all real duplicate rows, even though the synthetic queue is built to contain many other records sharing the same title/body prefixes.

chunk_findings.detail: The new scoped format still stores only one agent name per harness key, and `declare` overwrites the whole record. In the exact scenario the module docstring describes—coordinator shells and subagents descending from the same harness process, hence the same harness key—the first session’s identity is destroyed by another session’s declaration or withdrawal. For example, with the same repository and harness key, `declare(repo, "lead", "S_lead")` writes `lead\nsession:S_lead`; a later `declare(repo, "impl-ra", "S_sub")` overwrites it with `impl-ra\nsession:S_sub`. A subsequent read using `_matches` for `"S_lead"` sees only `{S_sub}` and does not match, so the lead has no stable identity (and if the read path returns the first line unfiltered, it is still attributed to `impl-ra`). Even `declare(repo, "lead", "S_sub")` for a second lead session removes `S_lead`, and `declare(repo, "", "S_sub")` unlinks the shared file, withdrawing the identity from the first session. This leaves the last writer in control and does not give the lead its own stable per-session identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/harness_identity.py:declare

chunk_findings.detail: The end-to-end CLI test launches `sys.executable -m ddflow` without making the repository importable in the child process. The test only prepends the repo root to `sys.path` inside the pytest process; the subprocess inherits the original environment (minus `DDFLOW_AGENT`) and the current working directory. If `ddflow` is not installed in the environment, or if an installed `ddflow` should not shadow the checkout under test, and pytest is invoked from outside the repository root, the child fails with `No module named ddflow` and the test fails at `assert r.returncode == 0` before it exercises identity. Example: with an uninstalled checkout at `/work/ddflow`, `cd /tmp && pytest /work/ddflow/tests/test_identity_lead.py` makes the subprocess unable to import the modified package.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_identity_lead.py:test_the_cli_identifies_derived_under_a_foreign_sessions_record

chunk_findings.detail: The tests assume `os.getppid()` names a readable process. `needs_proc` only checks `/proc/self/stat`, but `_write` immediately calls `H._stat(os.getppid())`. If pytest itself is PID 1 (common in a container whose main process is `pytest`), `os.getppid()` is `0`, `/proc/0/stat` does not exist, and `H._stat(0)` raises `FileNotFoundError` before any assertion runs. The skip guard should verify the parent pid used by the test is readable, or the test should use a pid guaranteed to exist.
